name: walkthrough
title: AI by Hand: cosine similarity, attention, softmax, and a forward pass
description: A step-by-step tour of the five Python blocks in the AI by Hand tutorial. You watch cosine similarity, attention, softmax with temperature, and a two-neuron forward pass each turn from paper arithmetic into running code.

steps.description: The program builds two vectors with numpy. Vector a is (2, 1, 0, 2) and vector b is (1, 1, 1, 1), the same two vectors you worked by hand on the page.
cosine_sim takes two vectors and returns their dot product divided by the product of their lengths. That is the cosine similarity formula from the page in one line of numpy.

steps.question: The program prints two cosine values. What is the second one, cos(a, 3a)?

steps.description: The two print calls show cos(a, b) and cos(a, 3a). Scaling a by 3 leaves its direction unchanged, so the second value is exactly 1.000.
Next the attention demo turns the four paper steps into code, with three tokens and a query, key and value vector for each.
Three dictionaries hold the vectors: q for the query, k for the key and v for the value of each token, river, bank and loan.

softmax subtracts the largest score before exponentiating, which keeps the numbers small; the comment in the code calls this numerical stability. It then divides each exponential by the sum, so the weights add to 1.
The scores are the bank query dotted with each key, divided by the square root of 2. softmax turns the scores into weights, and new_bank is the weighted sum of the value vectors.

steps.question: What does the program print for the softmax weights?

steps.description: This block runs the same softmax three times, once for each temperature in the page table.
The program imports numpy and sets three logits, 4.0, 2.0 and 1.0, the same logits the page uses.
For each temperature T the loop divides the logits by T, exponentiates, and divides by the sum. That is the temperature softmax from the page.
At this step the loop divides the exponentials by their sum, which turns them into probabilities that add to 1.

steps.question: What does the program print for T = 0.5?

steps.description: This block sweeps five temperatures over five tokens and reports each distribution's entropy.
softmax_temp repeats the temperature softmax in plain Python: divide by the temperature, subtract the largest value, exponentiate, and normalize.
entropy sums -p log p over the probabilities. The small 1e-10 added inside the log keeps the value finite when a probability is zero.
VOCAB lists the five tokens and LOGITS holds one raw score for each. Paris has the highest score, 4.5.
At this step the loop reaches line 21 and computes the entropy of the distribution for the current temperature.
The last block runs a small two-neuron ReLU network on the two inputs from the page tables.
W1 holds the two hidden-neuron weight rows, b1 their biases, and V with c the output weights and bias.
forward computes each hidden pre-activation, applies ReLU with max(0.0, p) to clip it at zero, then combines the hidden values into the output y.
At this step the code clips both pre-activations at zero to form h. For the first input the pre-activations are 0.5 and -0.5, so h becomes [0.5, 0.0].
